summary: Learn board-level cyber oversight, risk dashboards, and incident governance. Strengthen executive decision-making with TrainingCred.
lede: Board-level cybersecurity training helps directors and senior executives oversee cyber risk without needing to run security tools. Participants practice translating threats and control metrics into business exposure, reviewing risk appetite and investment priorities, and shaping incident escalation and board reporting. Scenario exercises include building dashboards, assessing maturity gaps, and designing incident decision trees.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for senior professionals who must oversee cybersecurity decisions, challenge management reporting, and support resilience without working as technical security specialists. Board directors overseeing cyber risk appetite and governance. Audit committee members reviewing cyber controls and assurance. Chief executive officers approving resilience priorities and reporting. Chief financial officers assessing cyber investment and loss exposure. Chief risk officers integrating cyber risk into enterprise risk. Chief information officers translating technical issues into business impact. Chief information security officers briefing boards on threats and control gaps. General counsel reviewing cyber incident disclosure and liability exposure. Heads of internal audit testing cyber governance and assurance. Non-executive directors asking sharper questions on security oversight.
prerequisites: Prerequisites required: No technical background is required. You should have experience in executive, board, audit, governance, finance, legal, risk, or operations roles, and a working familiarity with organizational strategy, risk reporting, and decision-making structures. The course is taught at operational application level for governance concepts and conceptual awareness level for technical topics such as SIEM, MFA, EDR, zero trust, and threat intelligence. No coding or programming is required. Participants should bring a laptop for template-based exercises and a willingness to review board papers, incident summaries, and cyber risk dashboards.
